ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Sick Visit — Eva Perón

code.originalText: Same-day sick visit for burning on passing urine during chemoradiation

text.paragraph: Burning on passing urine and cloudy urine for two days, in the third week of chemoradiation. [S]

Ms. Perón called the clinic and was seen the same day, with the visit in Spanish. She is in the third week of pelvic radiation and had her third weekly cisplatin dose four days ago. Since radiation began she has needed to pass urine a little more often, as she was told to expect. For two days she has had new burning, strong urgency, and cloudy, strong-smelling urine. She has had no fever, chills, back or side pain, or vomiting, and no blood in the urine. Her bowels are looser, twice a day, controlled with loperamide; nausea after cisplatin settles with ondansetron. The vaginal bleeding has nearly stopped. She is tired but still working half days. She has been coping, and the social worker has seen her once during treatment. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Tired but comfortable; temperature 37.2 °C, pulse 88, blood pressure 106/66
Soft; mild suprapubic tenderness; no other tenderness
Mild redness of the skin in the radiation field; no breakdown

Bleeding after intercourse and between periods, with heavier periods, for about four months, with tiredness and a dull pelvic ache. Never had cervical screening. Speculum examination shows a friable, exophytic mass about 4 cm across on the cervix that bleeds on contact. Punch biopsy, HPV test and cytology taken; urgent gynecologic oncology consultation booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem linked to her documented abnormal bleeding with anemia; superseded by the diagnosis at the consultation.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss: hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, mean cell volume 72 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL, with tiredness and breathlessness on stairs
S — Synthetic modern finding linked to her documented anemia from vaginal bleeding.

Invasive squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, HPV 16 positive: an exophytic tumor about 4.5 cm across with clinical involvement of the left parametrium, not reaching the pelvic wall; pelvic MRI and PET-CT ordered for FIGO 2018 staging. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented cervical cancer
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Acute cystitis during pelvic chemoradiation: two days of new burning, urgency and cloudy urine on top of mild radiation frequency, without fever or flank pain; urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite; culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; neutrophil count and kidney function normal; resolved
S — Synthetic acute infection; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Acute cystitis during chemoradiation (N30.00). New burning, urgency and cloudy urine with leukocyte esterase and nitrite on the dipstick point to a bladder infection rather than radiation cystitis alone. No fever or flank pain to suggest kidney infection. The neutrophil count is 2.6 x10^3/uL, so she is not neutropenic, and kidney function is normal (creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, eGFR 101), so nitrofurantoin is suitable. A urine culture was sent because radiation can mimic infection and a clear result guides any recurrence. [S]
Nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily with food for 5 days.
Fluids through the day.
Same-day call for fever of 38 °C or more, rigors, flank pain, or vomiting, because she is receiving chemotherapy.
Radiation oncology team informed; treatment continues without a break.
Culture result by phone.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix, FIGO 2018 stage IIB (C53.9). On schedule: week three of radiation, three of five cisplatin doses. Blood count adequate for the next dose (hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL, platelets 168). Diarrhea grade 1 on loperamide; nausea controlled. [S]
Continue chemoradiation as planned.
Continue loperamide and ondansetron as needed.

Iron deficiency anemia (D50.0). Hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL, holding above 10 during radiation. [S]
Continue ferrous sulfate.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Cervical Cancer (Version 1.2027); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia monograph (2026); International clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of acute uncomplicated cystitis and pyelonephritis in women: a 2010 update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America and the European Society for Microbiology and Infectious Diseases (2010)

Follow-up: Culture result by phone. Weekly on-treatment review with the oncology team; review here two weeks after brachytherapy. Next scheduled visit 2026-05-18: review two weeks after completing chemoradiation and brachytherapy: side effects, menopause symptoms, and survivorship care. [S]
